consensus_summary: Wheat primarily symbolizes the genuine people of God—true believers or children of the kingdom—gathered into God’s barn at the eschatological harvest/judgment, in contrast to tares or chaff.
book_summary: Wheat is the children of the kingdom, the good grain gathered into the barn at the harvest, opposite tares.
consensus_core_identification: children of the kingdom / true believers / righteous gathered at the final harvest
book_core_identification: children of the kingdom — the good grain gathered into the barn at the harvest
rationale: Both identify wheat with the same referent (children of the kingdom / good grain) in the same harvest context drawn from the identical primary texts; wording differences are immaterial and no boundary or case divergence appears.
strongest_objection: none; secondary senses (grain-of-wheat death, provision) exist in consensus but are treated as distinct and do not displace the shared primary core
